title: Overriding and Virtual Functions
learningObjectives: Identify relevant class/object relationships and access rules.
Apply the OOP concept in a small design.

understand.concept: A derived class can override a virtual base function with the same signature. Use override to have the compiler verify intent; virtual dispatch selects behavior based on dynamic type.
understand.whyItMatters: Overriding enables extensible behavior through common interfaces.
understand.explain: Keep signatures consistent, use override, and ensure base destructors are virtual for polymorphic ownership.

examples.title: Override with override
examples.code: struct Base{virtual void draw()const{}};\nstruct Circle:Base{void draw()const override{}};
examples.explanation: override makes compiler check the intended override.

examples.title: Virtual call
examples.code: struct Base{virtual int value()const{return 1;}};\nstruct Derived:Base{int value()const override{return 2;}};\nDerived d;Base& b=d;std::cout<<b.value();

examples.title: Virtual destructor
examples.explanation: Virtual destructor supports safe deletion through a base pointer.

examples.title: Signature mismatch caught
examples.code: struct Base{virtual void run(int){}};\nstruct Derived:Base{void run(double) override {} }; // compile error
examples.explanation: override detects that parameter signature does not match.

examples.title: Default virtual implementation
examples.explanation: A virtual function can provide a default implementation.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze the five Overriding and Virtual Functions examples. Identify class responsibilities, interface, object state, lifetime and dispatch behavior where relevant.
practise.independentTask: Design a small C++ program demonstrating overriding and virtual functions in a practical domain. Use clear public operations, appropriate access control, and tests for expected behavior and edge cases.
hints: Start by listing responsibilities and objects.
Keep internal state protected where needed.
Initialize objects deliberately and understand lifetime.
Use inheritance only for substitutable relationships.
Test behavior through the public interface.

questions.explanation: override checks that a virtual function is overridden.

questions.prompt: Base destructor should be virtual for?
questions.explanation: Virtual destructor supports correct derived cleanup.

questions.prompt: Can virtual function have base implementation?
questions.explanation: Virtual functions may provide default behavior.
